title: MCP `query_records` silently ignores unknown sort/filter keys while `fields` hard-errors on unknown values
body:
**Finding from a video-studio recording spike (steedos-labs/video-studio#274). Not claiming; filed for the product team to triage.**

## What happens

On objectstack **17.3.0** (hotcrm `d01d27b`), calling the MCP tool `query_records` with an unsupported sort key, e.g.

```json
{"objectName":"crm_opportunity","sort":"-amount","limit":3}
```

returns `HTTP 200` with an **unsorted** result set. No error, no warning. The supported form is `orderBy:[{"field":"amount","order":"desc"}]`.

## Why it matters

This is inconsistent with the same tool's own handling of `fields`, which **rejects** unknown values with an explicit rationale ("dropping an unknown one silently answered a NARROWER projection with a WIDER one"). The identical argument applies to sort/filter keys: a silently dropped sort answers a **differently ordered** result set than the caller asked for, and an LLM caller has no way to detect it. In our test the agent confidently reported the first N rows as "the top N opportunities by amount".

Impact: agent-facing correctness. An AI client that mis-guesses a parameter name gets plausible-looking wrong answers instead of an error.

## Suggested fix

Reject unknown top-level keys in `query_records` arguments (or at minimum unknown sort/filter keys), matching the existing `fields` behaviour.

## Repro context

- hotcrm `main` @ `d01d27b`, `@objectstack/* 17.3.0`, `pnpm dev` on port 4001
- MCP via `x-api-key` minted with `POST /api/v1/keys`
- `tools/list` → 11 tools; `query_records` with `sort:'-amount'` → 200, rows in seed order
